answer: The data objects are tagged `#meta/library/remote`. They sit inside a repository page, which is itself tagged `#meta/repository`.
block:
--- Library/Development.md ---
Decorate your library with frontmatter | Create a repository
If you develop a few libraries, it may be good to make them more discoverable. To do so, you can group them in a [[Repository|Repository]].

For this, create another page in your space, this time under `Repository/`, e.g. `Repository/myuser` and tag it with `#meta/repository`.

In the page body, put a list of all your libraries, encoded as [[Tag/data|data objects]] as follows:

    ---
    tags: meta/repository
    ---
    This is my curated list of awesome libraries!

    ```#meta/library/remote
    name: Library1
    description: This is my first awesome library
    website: http://url.com/to/docs
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library1.md
    ---
    name: Library2
    description: This is my second awesome library
    uri: https://github.com/myuser/silverbullet-libraries/blob/main/Library2.md
    ```

Required keys are:
* `name`: a descriptive name of your library.
  **Note**: this name is _not_ used as an installation location, the installation location is determined by the `name` key in the library itself.

--- Library/Development.md ---
Decorate your library with frontmatter | Create a repository
* `uri`: The URI to install the library from.

Additional recommended keys are:
* `description`: a more elaborate description of the library and its functionality
* `author`: who developed this library
* `website`: a website URL for more information

Now share this repo page using [[Share]] to the same github repo (or any other, it doesn’t really matter), and call it `REPO.md` (by convention).

Then announce to the [community](https://community.silverbullet.md/c/plugs-libraries/14) that your repo is open for business and they can add it via the `Library: Add Repository` command (using the same `share.uri` set in your frontmatter).

--- Repository.md ---
Repository
Repositories are a collection of _pointers_ to [[Library|Libraries]] to install. Their purpose is to offer a curated list of libraries to install.

By default, SilverBullet ships with two repositories: [[^Repositories/Std]] with a curated selection of community libraries, and [[^Repositories/SilverBulletMD]] with optional libraries maintained by the SilverBullet project. More can be installed via the [[Workbench/Libraries|Library Manager]].

The built-in repositories update like any other: the first update stores a copy in your space, which from then on takes the place of the shipped version. Deleting that copy brings the shipped version back, so built-in repositories can’t be removed.

Repositories are implemented on top of a few SilverBullet mechanisms, specifically they are simply [[Meta Page|Meta Pages]] tagged with `#meta/repository` that contain [[Tag/data|data objects]] tagged with `#meta/library/remote` with a `name` and `uri` attribute. Libraries are kept up to date using the [[Share]] mechanism.

--- Virtual Pages.md ---
How it works | Built-in virtual pages > Tag pages
The most commonly used virtual pages are **tag pages**. When you click a hashtag like `#project`, SilverBullet navigates to `tag:project`, which is a virtual page that lists all objects with that tag — grouped by type (pages, tasks, items, data, etc.).

Tag pages are defined in the standard library and work out of the box. You can override the default tag page by defining your own `virtualPage.define` with the pattern `tag:(.+)`.

--- Workbench/Libraries.md ---
Checking for updates
* **Available**: the libraries your repositories offer, grouped by repository, with the recommended Std repository first. **Install** puts one in your space. Available library titles open their configured website. When no website is configured, the title opens the library’s source page using the browser URL for its URI (for example, expanding a `github:` URI to its GitHub file page).
* **Repositories**: the [[Repository|repositories]] you added, with **Update all** to refresh all of them. Any that fail are listed with the reason. The built-in repositories (Std and SilverBulletMD) update like the others but can’t be removed.

An installed library or repository row shows its share URI. Its context menu offers:
* *Update*: pulls the latest version from its source. When you edited a library here and its source changed too, it asks before replacing your edits.
